title: Glock leads a BMW one-two-three in Zandvoort Race 1
dek: Timo Glock won DTM Race 1 at Zandvoort from pole by 0.178s for BMW Team RMG, completing a BMW podium sweep, while René Rast took the points lead after Mattias Ekström's gravel trip.

chapters.title: Round six opens with Audi on top and Mercedes on the way out
text: The DTM reached Zandvoort for round six on 19–20 August with Audi's Mattias Ekström leading the championship on 113 points, one clear of his team-mate René Rast on 112, and Mercedes' Lucas Auer third on 99. It was the first meeting since Mercedes announced that it would leave the series at the end of 2018. The previous round at Moscow had been won by Rast in Race 1 and by Mercedes' Maro Engel in Race 2, after he started from 17th on the grid.

The 4.307km circuit through the dunes offers few places to overtake, which put the emphasis on qualifying, on strategy and on tyre wear: every driver had a mandatory pit stop, and BMW's sporting director Jens Marquardt would later call tyre management the real challenge of the weekend. BMW had won only twice all season, at the Norisring, and Maxime Martin was its best-placed driver, fifth on 78 points.

chapters.title: Four BMWs on the front two rows as the rain arrives
text: Qualifying was a BMW exercise. Timo Glock set 1m27.823s on his first flying lap and nobody could beat it: all 18 cars came in for fresh tyres and went back out early because rain threatened, but a shower arrived before the second runs could produce improvements and the order at the top stayed as it was. It was Glock's second pole of the season, after Hockenheim Race 2.

Augusto Farfus was second, 0.084s slower, followed by Glock's other team-mate Marco Wittmann on 1m28.065s and Maxime Martin on 1m28.155s, giving BMW the first four places on the grid. Rast was fifth on 1m28.287s as the best Audi, ahead of Loïc Duval on 1m28.331s and Tom Blomqvist, seventh on 1m28.351s. Gary Paffett was the only Mercedes in the top ten, eighth on 1m28.375s.

Mike Rockenfeller qualified ninth and Ekström, the championship leader, tenth on 1m28.547s. Paul di Resta, Robert Wickens, Engel, Nico Müller and Jamie Green filled 11th to 15th. Auer, third in the standings, could manage only 16th on 1m28.861s, ahead of Bruno Spengler on 1m28.875s and Edoardo Mortara, last of the 18 cars, 1.160s off the pole time.

chapters.title: Glock gets away and the BMW trio pulls clear
text: Glock made a strong start and kept the lead, with Wittmann and Martin both getting past Farfus in the first corners to leave the order as Glock, Wittmann, Martin, Farfus. The top three soon pulled clear, and Rast, running fifth behind four BMWs, spent the opening laps bottled up behind Farfus. He tried a move early on, but Farfus held position. Audi's motorsport chief Dieter Gass later said Rast had lost too much time there.

Two drivers gambled at the end of the first lap. Blomqvist and Rockenfeller both made their mandatory stop immediately and dropped to the back of the field. For Rockenfeller, who had qualified ninth, it proved the better strategy, and he went on to finish fourth. Blomqvist, who had started seventh, completed only 17 laps.

chapters.title: Rast stays out, Ekström goes into the gravel
text: Most of the field came in during the first ten laps. Wittmann and Martin stopped first among the leaders and Glock followed, restoring the same order, while Farfus dropped back through the field after his own stop. That left Rast leading the race on old tyres, and he stayed out until around lap 18. He rejoined in traffic behind di Resta's Mercedes, could not find a way past, and later slipped behind Paffett as well. He still set the fastest lap of the race, a 1m30.160s on lap 21.

Ekström's afternoon went wrong right after his stop. On cold tyres he slid into the gravel at Tarzan, the first corner, dragged stones back onto the track and spun a moment later. He later made a second call at the pits and completed 34 of the 37 laps, three laps down. Duval, who had picked up a five-second stop penalty for a jump start, and Spengler both ran very long first stints and did not stop until the last ten laps. Spengler rejoined 14th. Auer, meanwhile, had run into the gravel after touching Müller early on, and finished 15th.

chapters.title: Glock holds off Wittmann by 0.178 seconds
text: Once the late stops were done Glock was back in front of Wittmann and Martin, and that is how they finished after 37 laps: Glock first, Wittmann 0.178s behind and Martin 0.840s back. It was Glock's first win of the season and the fourth of his DTM career, and he said afterwards that vibrations from a front tyre had made the closing laps a struggle.

Martin had to defend hard against the Audis in the closing stages. Rockenfeller, who had worked his way from ninth on the grid, spent many laps behind the BMW with Jamie Green right behind him, but neither Audi could find a way past. Rockenfeller finished fourth, 2.530s behind Glock, with Green fifth after starting 15th. Farfus was sixth, ahead of di Resta, the best Mercedes, and Paffett.

Rast was ninth, 5.911s behind, but the two points were enough to put him one ahead of Ekström in the standings, 114 to 113, with Auer on 99 and Glock back up to fourth on 98. Müller took the last point in tenth, holding off Wickens and Mortara. Engel, who had also run through the gravel on the opening lap, was 16th.

facts.v: Glock beat Wittmann by 0.178s and Martin finished 0.840s behind to complete a BMW one-two-three.
